bifrost: none (no app-facing API). Test rig only: tools/arch-vm.sh, docs/arch-x86-vm.md
summary: Apple's Hypervisor framework is a C API that lets sandboxed user-space apps create VMs and vCPUs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. BifrOSt exposes no VM API to apps; QEMU/KVM is used only as a developer test rig for running the shell in an Arch guest, and the SDK's host module reads only the task's memory footprint from /proc.

features.note: Apps have no way to create a VM. A desktop SDK would not normally offer this, and apps run under the bubblewrap sandbox (springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs).
No vCPU abstraction exists in the SDK or the shell.

features.feature: Memory mapping into guest physical address space
features.note: The guest-memory mapping is only the Arch VM under QEMU, not an app API.
Only guest timers inside the QEMU VM are used; no SDK surface.

features.bifrost: none for hypervisor capabilities; springboard/core/src/host.rs is a different thing (host CPU and memory statistics)
features.note: host.rs does not report virtualisation support, so an app could not learn whether a hypervisor is available.

features.apple: GIC functions and registers, hv_vm_add_pio_notifier, hv_vcpu_apic_* functions
features.note: Device emulation for guests does not exist in BifrOSt. Only the QEMU test VM provides it.
BifrOSt has no entitlement model. App isolation is in springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs and docs/app-isolation.md.

features.feature: Developer test rig: Arch Linux guest under QEMU/KVM
features.apple: not applicable (Apple's framework is an app API)
features.note: Developer tooling only. It runs the shell on tty1 in a KVM guest. It is not an SDK feature and no app can use it.

gaps: No app-facing VM API. Decision: a desktop SDK does not expose hypervisors to apps, so the Hypervisor framework is marked n/a rather than gap. Revisit only if a VM-hosting app (for example a Linux VM app) is planned.
The shell cannot report whether KVM or a hypervisor is available. host.rs covers CPU and memory statistics only.
